items.title: Anthropic files to sell shares on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT
items.why: Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI models, publicly filed for a stock market listing in the US on Monday. Its filing shows revenue of $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026 and a net loss of $80.7 billion, mostly from a non-cash charge. No valuation was given.
items.matters: It could be one of the largest share sales ever; reports say the listing is aimed for mid-November.

items.title: Egypt's pound falls to a record low of 56 to the dollar
items.why: The Egyptian pound fell to a record 56 per US dollar on Monday, LSEG data cited by Reuters show, having first passed 55 on 22 October. Analysts quoted by Enterprise blame foreign investors selling Egyptian debt, costly energy and wheat imports, and regional conflict.
items.matters: A weaker pound makes imported food and fuel dearer in Egypt; the central bank decides on interest rates on Thursday.

items.title: Saudi-led coalition says it struck Houthi missile sites in Yemen
items.why: The coalition backing Yemen's government says it destroyed five missile-storage tunnels, four ballistic missile launchers and a depot in Houthi-held areas on Monday. The Houthis say they fired a missile at Riyadh's airport; Saudi air defences say they intercepted a missile aimed at the city.
items.matters: Fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis has escalated since a 2022 truce collapsed last month.

items.title: Nurse killed while responding to Ebola alert in DR Congo
items.why: Attackers killed a nurse and badly injured another responder in Bafwasende, in DR Congo's Tshopo province, on Saturday. Health officials say the attackers accused them of spreading Ebola, which officials call a rumour. The WHO and UN condemned the attack.
items.matters: Attacks on health workers are slowing the response to Congo's deadliest Ebola outbreak, officials say.

items.title: Cyclone Arnab strengthens; red alert issued for India's east coast
items.why: Cyclone Arnab is expected to become a very severe cyclonic storm and cross Andhra Pradesh's coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam on the morning of 28 October, India's weather office says, with gusts up to 140 km/h. It has issued a red alert for coastal Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha.
items.matters: Andhra Pradesh officials say 570,000 people are vulnerable; evacuations and a fishing ban are under way.
items.changed: Updated: the weather office now expects a very severe storm and has issued a red alert

items.title: Asian shares mostly fall as investors await tech results and rate decisions
items.why: Tokyo's Nikkei closed 0.8% lower on Monday, its third daily fall, led by chip stocks, and Seoul's Kospi fell 1.5%. Hong Kong and Shanghai edged up. Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Samsung and SK hynix report results this week, and the US, Japanese and European central banks decide on interest rates.
items.matters: Investors want proof that huge spending on AI is paying off, and rate decisions affect loans and savings worldwide.

items.title: Jordan arrests three suspects over deadly attack on Karak church
items.why: Jordanian security forces arrested three men on Monday after a three-hour gunfight in a village in Karak, south of Amman, police say. They are suspected of Friday's attack on a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church, in which Jordan's health ministry says eight people were killed; some reports say nine.
items.matters: King Abdullah has called it terrorism and ordered a review of how security forces respond to such attacks.

items.title: Eric Bauza, voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, dies at 46
items.why: The Canadian-born voice actor Eric Bauza died suddenly on Sunday 25 October, his manager said. He was the modern voice of Looney Tunes characters including Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Porky Pig and Tweety, and won three Children's and Family Emmy awards.
items.matters: His voices reached children around the world through Looney Tunes cartoons, films and games.

items.title: Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials meet Iran's military chief in Tehran
items.why: Saudi Arabia's defence minister, Pakistan's army chief and Turkey's intelligence chief met Iran's top military official in Tehran on Monday, reports say. On Sunday President Trump said he was choosing between a deal and action to 'finish them off', but ruled out strikes that day.
items.matters: The three countries signed a mutual defence pact in August; Saudi officials say the visit aims to calm the crisis.
items.changed: Updated: the meeting has now taken place

items.title: Oil eases from six-month high as Qatar mediates with Iran
items.why: Brent crude fell about 1–2% on Monday to around $115 a barrel, after Qatari mediators visited Tehran on Sunday to try to ease tensions with the US, Reuters reports. Brent had risen more than 6% last week, its highest weekly close since 2022.
items.matters: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia keep supply worries alive, Reuters reports, so fuel and shipping costs stay high.

items.title: Lula wins fourth term in Brazil; Flávio Bolsonaro demands annulment
items.why: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Sunday's run-off with about 51.8% of valid votes to 48.2% for Flávio Bolsonaro, official results show. Bolsonaro, who led the first round, said it was 'impossible to recognise the results' after a court extended voting hours, and will seek annulment.
items.matters: Lula, 80, wins an unprecedented fourth term, Brazil's electoral court says, and would serve until 2030.

items.title: Serbia's Vučić concedes election defeat to student-led movement
items.why: Aleksandar Vučić conceded on Sunday night that his Serbian Progressive Party had lost the snap parliamentary election to the Student List, which grew out of two years of anti-corruption protests. Vučić said early results gave the students 135 to 140 of 250 seats. Turnout was close to 70%.
items.matters: It would end Vučić's long hold on power; final official results are still to come.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli wins US Grand Prix and nears first Formula 1 title
items.why: Italy's Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes won the United States Grand Prix in Austin, Texas, on 25 October, his ninth win of the season. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was second and Red Bull's Max Verstappen third. Antonelli now leads by 123 points with 125 left to win.
items.matters: A top-nine finish at the Mexico City Grand Prix on 1 November would give him the drivers' title, Sky Sports says.

items.title: Musk says SpaceX has borrowed $40 billion to buy AI chips
items.why: Elon Musk said on Sunday, in a post on X, that SpaceX had closed $40 billion of debt financing, mainly to buy graphics chips arriving in early 2027. He warned that lenders have largely stopped funding 'neocloud' firms that only rent out AI computing power, predicting failures among them.
items.matters: Doubts over how AI companies pay for their huge spending have hit share prices worldwide in recent weeks.

items.title: Residents say 50 killed in gunmen's attack on Nigerian village
items.why: Armed men on motorcycles attacked Binnari village in Nigeria's Taraba State on Friday. Police first confirmed 10 deaths; residents say 50 bodies have now been found, many in a river where people drowned while fleeing. Amnesty International says the toll may be as high as 52.

items.title: Uganda orders 21-day quarantine for citizens returning from DR Congo
items.why: Uganda's health minister, Chris Baryomunsi, said on 25 October that citizens returning from the Democratic Republic of Congo must quarantine for 21 days, at their own cost. Kenya reported its second Ebola death on 23 October; it has nine cases, all in one cluster.
items.matters: The first patients in Kenya and Nigeria both passed through Uganda; WHO counted 9,704 cases in DR Congo by 20 October.

items.title: Mbappé scores twice as Real Madrid beat leaders Barcelona 2-1
items.why: Kylian Mbappé scored in the 41st and 87th minutes as Real Madrid won 2-1 at Barcelona's Camp Nou on 25 October, after Raphinha had equalised. It ended Barcelona's run of nine straight league wins and was their first defeat of the Spanish season.
items.matters: Barcelona still top La Liga on 27 points, ahead of Atlético Madrid on 25 and Real Madrid on 24.

items.title: Shadab Khan's century and record last-wicket stand lift Pakistan past England
items.why: Pakistan were 154 for nine chasing 242 in Lahore on 25 October when Shadab Khan and Haris Rauf added an unbeaten 89, the highest tenth-wicket stand in a winning one-day chase. Shadab made 113 not out as Pakistan won by one wicket.
items.matters: Pakistan reach the tri-series final on 31 October; England must beat Sri Lanka on 29 October to stay in contention.

items.title: Algeria approves sending troops to Niger, its first foreign deployment since 1973
items.why: Algeria's parliament voted on Sunday to send troops to neighbouring Niger to protect energy facilities, including Algerian oil sites. AFP reports 148 of 174 senators backed it. The number of soldiers and where they will go have not been announced.
items.matters: Algeria has not sent soldiers abroad since it backed Egypt in the 1973 Arab-Israeli war.

items.title: Storms Boelo and Austen leave over 150,000 European homes without power
items.why: Two storms crossed north-western Europe within 24 hours over the weekend. Scottish police say a man died when a tree fell on him in Dumfries and Galloway on Sunday. More than 150,000 homes in the UK, France and Germany were without power on Sunday, AFP reports.
items.matters: Flood warnings remain in parts of Scotland and England, and travel by rail, ferry and air was disrupted.

items.title: Bangladesh records its highest daily dengue admissions this year
items.why: Bangladesh's health directorate says 2,249 dengue patients were admitted to hospital in the 24 hours to 8am on 25 October, the most in a single day this year. The year's death toll reached 384, including 139 in October.
items.matters: Dengue usually peaks in Bangladesh's June–September monsoon, but this year cases are still rising in October.

items.title: Offshore drilling rig sinks off Gabon with 115 people on board
items.why: Borr Drilling's Prospector 5 rig sank off Mayumba, Gabon, on Saturday evening. The company and Gabon's government say 110 people are safe and five missing; Reuters, citing unnamed sources, reports one dead and four missing. Borr says a leg punched through the seabed, making the rig unstable.
items.matters: Gabon has ordered a technical investigation; the ministry says no pollution has been seen so far.
items.changed: Updated: Borr Drilling gives a first explanation for the sinking

items.title: Rain cancels last MotoGP race at Australia's Phillip Island
items.why: Organisers called off the Australian MotoGP in Victoria, Australia, on 25 October because poor visibility grounded the medical helicopter. Marc Márquez, who won Saturday's sprint, leads the championship by 10 points from Jorge Martín, who fractured his arm in a crash.
items.matters: Four rounds remain, starting in Malaysia next weekend; from 2027 the Australian round moves to a street circuit in Adelaide.

items.title: Indian painter Jogen Chowdhury dies in Kolkata at 87
items.why: The Indian painter Jogen Chowdhury died in hospital in Kolkata on Sunday 25 October, aged 87, after about 14 months with a rare blood cancer, the hospital said. Born in 1939 in what is now Bangladesh, he also sat in India's upper house of parliament from 2014 to 2020.
items.matters: His work, known for its flowing lines and cross-hatching, hangs in public buildings including India's presidential palace.

items.title: Bus and lorry collide on Kenyan highway, killing at least 24
items.why: A church bus and a lorry collided head-on on the Nairobi–Mombasa highway near Mtito Andei, Kenya, on Sunday morning. At least 24 people died and 24 were injured, Makueni county officials say. Officials suspect improper overtaking.
items.matters: President Ruto has ordered inspections of all public service vehicles; it is the highway's second deadly crash in three weeks.

items.title: Valkyries beat Dream 67-62 to level WNBA Finals at 2-2
items.why: The Golden State Valkyries won 67-62 in Atlanta on Saturday 24 October to level the best-of-seven WNBA Finals with the Atlanta Dream at 2-2. They held Angel Reese to eight points; Gabby Williams scored 17. Game 5 is in San Francisco on Monday night.
items.matters: Where Game 6 will be played in Atlanta is still undecided because the larger arena used earlier is booked, ESPN reports.

items.title: Shark trapped in Busan canal moves out into wider port waters
items.why: Bukangi, an endangered 3-metre dusky shark that spent over a month in a canal in Busan, South Korea, has been spotted about 2 km away near the port's passenger terminal, the National Institute of Fisheries Science said on 24 and 25 October. It has not yet reached open sea.
items.matters: Officials say the shark looks healthy and plan no further rescue attempts, though one US expert fears chronic stress.

items.title: Jamaican ska and reggae pioneer Derrick Harriott dies at 87
items.why: Derrick Harriott, the Jamaican singer and producer whose career spanned ska, rocksteady and reggae, died at his home on Saturday 24 October, aged 87, Jamaican newspapers report. His hits included 'The Loser', and he produced records for artists such as Dennis Brown and Big Youth.
items.matters: He helped shape early reggae and dub, music now heard far beyond Jamaica.

items.changed: Updated: thousands displaced in Hebron operation; crossings closed for election day
items.title: Israeli raid in Hebron displaces thousands, city says; crossings shut for vote
items.why: Israeli forces began a days-long operation in Hebron after Friday's killing of two soldiers at a nearby checkpoint. The army says about 40 people were detained; Hebron's municipality says about 2,400 residents were displaced. All West Bank crossings into Israel close for Tuesday's election.
items.matters: Defence Minister Israel Katz says residents cannot return until the army finishes; Israelis vote on Tuesday, 27 October.

items.changed: Updated: final bids topped 22 times the shares on offer
items.title: India's Jio Platforms share sale draws a record 10 million applications
items.why: Bidding closed on Friday for the first share sale by Jio Platforms, Mukesh Ambani's telecoms and digital firm, which is raising about $3.2bn. Investors bid for more than 22 times the shares on offer, Reuters reports, and Indian exchanges recorded more than 10 million applications, a record.
items.matters: Shares were due to be allotted on 26 October and start trading on 28 October, valuing the company at about $108bn.
